generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The `CaseEagerEvaluator` continues to use range-based copies (`builder.copyFrom(lhs, p, p + 1)`) for single positions. The accompanying comment explicitly notes that this is "quite slow" and suggests using single-valued copies—an API that has been introduced in this chapter across all `BlockBuilder` implementations. This should be updated to use the new `copyFrom(block, position)` methods for better performance.

In the `perPosition` implementation of the lazy evaluators (e.g., `CoalesceBooleanLazyEvaluator`), there is an inconsistency in how values are copied into the result builder. The first block (`lastFullBlock`) is copied using a range-based call (`result.copyFrom(lastFullBlock, p, p + 1)`), while subsequent blocks are copied using the new single-position API (`result.copyFrom(block, 0)`). Since `lastFullBlock` is already known not to be a vector at this stage, the range-based call is less direct and should be replaced with the single-position `copyFrom` for consistency and clarity.

review_comment:
This is important for catching the case where your value is `null`, but the rest of the block isn't null. I had an off-by-one error in the evaluators somewhere that the standard tests weren't catching and this does.

It's not clear to me if this is worth pulling to the top level class.

This `switch` will fail to compile if you make a new type and don't include it. We intend for COALESCE to work for all types. If you are building a new type then you can stub it out as you go like you'll do with a few other evaluators.

I could intentionally didn't make a version of this thing in `Block.Builder` because I:
1. Want you to know if you need a scratch.
2. Want you to specialize on each type in the tight loops.
